transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-11 10:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Olivia (Nimbus VP Eng), Ethan (Nimbus SRE), Priya (Nimbus Security), Samir (Nimbus Platform)

Summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Focus on networking issues observed in last stress run, review of latency/throughput numbers, plan for upcoming runtime upgrade and rollback/observability needs.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining - I think we have a pretty full agenda, quick status, then dive into the perf numbers, networking, and the upgrade plan. Olivia - want to kick off with any priority items from Nimbus?
00:18 Olivia (Nimbus): Yeah thanks, um so main thing from our side is the stress run on Tuesday, we saw some intermittent route flaps which caused failed token requests to some instances, so that bubbled up as 502s for about a minute at peak. We isolated it to, uh, something with the NLB health checks but not 100% sure. Ethan's been digging.
00:34 Ethan (Nimbus): Yeah, the NLB was cycling targets, which is what made some requests route to an older runtime version that doesn't have the KV caching patch. So when the requests hit that node, latency spiked and a few calls timed out. We also noticed increased tail at seq lengths ~1024.
00:50 Diego (Redwood): Okay that aligns with a couple of things we saw on our end - during the stress test we showed a small percentage of instances not draining properly when they were marked unhealthy; that fed into our autoscaler behavior. We're suspecting a misconfigured health check timeout in the NLB.
01:06 Lena (Redwood): Also to call out - the instances that were hit had older kernel + runtime combo; they didn't have the memory allocator fix we pushed in the last hotfix. If traffic goes to them, you can get worse KV cache eviction behavior.
01:20 Priya (Nimbus): From security, we want to make sure any routing changes keep traffic in our private subnets; we can't have egress to public infra for customer data. Is Redwood still ok using private endpoints only?
01:34 Maya (Redwood): Yes - for the pilot we're using VPC peering and private endpoints. There is an optional path that uses NAT for model downloads and image pulls; we recommended configuring egress via a controlled NAT gateway with strict rules. We'll share a diagram with exact flows.
01:49 Samir (Nimbus): Can you add where KMS/EKM traffic flows? We need to validate firewall rules for the customer-managed key service.
01:56 Maya (Redwood): Absolutely - we'll include KMS endpoints and port ranges in the diagram. On the security docs side, we also have the SOC2 summary and audit log detail that we can send.
02:10 Olivia (Nimbus): Great, thanks.

02:22 Diego (Redwood): I pulled the numbers from Tuesday's run: average latency (p50) for text-gen across the cluster was 62ms for seq=256, p95 at 210ms; for seq=1024 p50 ~420ms, p95 ~1.6s, but interestingly the p99 was spiking to 4s when requests hit those older nodes. KV cache hit rate overall is 82%, but for the subset of requests that routed incorrectly it dropped to ~28%.
02:46 Ethan (Nimbus): That matches our traces - you can see the sudden jump in CPU and mem on the old nodes. We correlated traces to the NLB events.
02:55 Lena (Redwood): Proposed short-term mitigation: tighten NLB health timeout and ensure graceful drain is >= 60s before removal, plus set the instance update policy to do a gradual rotation. Longer-term, we recommend pinning a canary lane for the runtime upgrade.
03:12 Priya (Nimbus): On upgrades - what's the rollback story if the new runtime increases tail latency or breaks our external tracing? We need an explicit rollback runbook.
03:20 Diego (Redwood): We can provide a rollback runbook - it's mostly automatable: mark canary instances unhealthy, spin up previous runtime images in the same pool, and route traffic back. We'll also provide scripts to reinitialize KV caches so you don't see cold-cache regressions. We'll schedule a dry-run on a dev cluster before doing prod.
03:40 Maya (Redwood): Diego - can you own the runbook and the dry-run?
03:44 Diego (Redwood): Yep, I'll own it and I'll also produce flamegraphs from the seq=1024 runs.
03:48 Ethan (Nimbus): I'll share the VPC peering CIDRs and the NACL rules by Friday - that should make it easier to validate route tables.
03:56 Maya (Redwood): Thank you. A few quick asks from Redwood: please attach the stress test logs (we need the raw traces) and the NLB event window. That will help us reproduce.
04:05 Olivia (Nimbus): We'll upload the logs to the shared workspace.

04:18 Lena (Redwood): On the performance tuning side - we measured batch sizes. For your workload, batching of 8 achieved the best cost-latency tradeoff at seq=256, but for seq=1024 the sweet spot was smaller batch sizes of 3-4 to avoid seq-length amplification on KV cache misses. We also saw benefit from increasing token cache TTL for long-running sessions.
04:42 Samir (Nimbus): Is the cache persistent across instance restarts or does it warm up? Persistent would be great but we expect some cold starts.
04:50 Lena (Redwood): At the moment it's an in-memory KV cache tied to the instance; persistent cache is an advanced option but not enabled in the pilot. Our mitigation is to stagger restarts and pre-warm canary nodes.
05:04 Priya (Nimbus): For security acceptance we need audit logs that show model access and key usage for every generation request. Does Redwood's Private control-plane provide that?
05:14 Maya (Redwood): Yes - we emit audit logs for request metadata, model versions, and KMS usage; we can add the retention window details. We also have SAML SSO integration for RBAC.
05:25 Priya (Nimbus): Good - please send the doc on retention and how to pull logs.
05:29 Maya (Redwood): Will do.

05:40 Diego (Redwood): Quick note about routing fallbacks - we have policy options: latency-first (route to fastest pool), cost-first (route to cheaper model variants), and strict-isolation (no cross-pool fallbacks). For Nimbus pilot we defaulted to latency-first with a fallback to identical model variant on dedicated lane; we can switch to strict-isolation if that's required for compliance.
06:05 Olivia (Nimbus): For now we'd prefer strict-isolation for any Prod-facing endpoints but are ok with latency-first for dev. We'll formalize which endpoints are considered Prod.
06:16 Maya (Redwood): Perfect - we'll map that in the runbook.

06:28 Lena (Redwood): Regarding the upcoming runtime upgrade: we're planning to roll the new runtime (v1.12.0) next Wednesday in a canary for 10% of traffic for 2 hours, then a 30% for 4 hours, then full. The upgrade includes the KV caching fixes and a new attention kernel that reduces tail latency by ~8% on average in our internal tests.
06:48 Ethan (Nimbus): Any expected downtime?
06:50 Diego (Redwood): No planned downtime, only targeted restarts; that's why the graceful drain and canary are important. But we will schedule the dry-run in your dev VPC first.
06:59 Priya (Nimbus): We want an email escalation plan in case we need an immediate rollback. Also a defined SLA for how fast you can switch lanes.
07:08 Maya (Redwood): We'll add escalation contacts and expected times - Diego will own the rollback script; Maya will be primary contact and Lena will be on-call for the kernel issues.

07:20 Diego (Redwood): From open items on my side - I need the exact trace IDs for the high tail samples so I can correlate with flamegraphs; if you can't pull them, send the raw logs and we'll do it.
07:32 Ethan (Nimbus): We'll include trace IDs in the zip.
07:35 Olivia (Nimbus): Quick check on pricing - Maya, you mentioned Dedicated lanes pricing tiers in the last sync. Can you resend the breakdown for reserved capacity vs burst pricing?
07:45 Maya (Redwood): Yep, I'll send a detailed break down with examples based on your weekly peak QPS.
07:50 Samir (Nimbus): One last infra question - do we need special IAM for the instances for KMS access or does Redwood use an intermediate proxy?
07:58 Maya (Redwood): For this pilot we use your KMS via a mutual-auth TLS connection; the instances authenticate via the control plane to the KMS endpoint. We'll outline the minimal IAM rules needed.
08:10 Priya (Nimbus): Also confirm key rotation window - we need to ensure keys rotate quarterly and that rotating doesn't break running sessions.
08:18 Diego (Redwood): We'll validate rotation and include tests in the dry-run.

08:30 Maya (Redwood): Alright let's recap action items and next steps. Diego will own rollback/runbook and flamegraphs; Ethan will provide network/NLB logs and CIDRs; Priya will enumerate compliance doc asks; Maya will send pricing and security docs. We agreed to run a dev dry-run for the upgrade on Monday, March 16th.
08:52 Olivia (Nimbus): That sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?
08:56 Maya (Redwood): None - just need the logs and CIDR info.
08:59 Olivia (Nimbus): We'll get those to you.
09:05 Maya (Redwood): Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the shared workspace and I'll drop the network diagram by Friday.
09:12 Meeting end.
